What happens when a customer asks?

items.title: The problem
items.text: Sam is a very good plumber, and his phone is quiet.

items.title: The question
items.text: A customer has a leak. She asks an engine, not Sam: who should I call?

items.title: How engines decide
items.text: Three questions. Can I read it? Do others confirm it? Do people choose it?

items.title: The fix
items.text: We raise all three: what the site says, what others confirm, what people pick.

items.title: The answer
items.text: Same question. Now every engine has a reason to name Sam.

settings.editor: Sam is a drawing, not a client. Read the equation in full

settings.title: Be the answer: how an engine decides who to name
settings.caption: Be the answer. Narrated, with captions. Written by Thomas D'Souza, Founder.
settings.fallback: Your browser does not play video. The five chapters beside it tell the same story.
settings.description: A narrated animated film: a customer asks an engine who to call, the engine asks three things (can I read it, do others confirm it, do people choose it), and raising all three changes the answer.
settings.transcript: This is Sam. He's the best plumber in town. But his phone is quiet. When a customer has a leak, she doesn't call Sam. She asks Google, Maps or ChatGPT: who should I call? Every engine decides the same way. It asks three things. Can I read what this business does? Do other sources confirm it? Do real people choose it? The three multiply. If one is zero, the answer is zero. So the engine names someone else. We fix all three. Read: Sam's site now says plainly what he does, where, and for whom. Confirm: listings, reviews and mentions that say the same thing. Choose: a listing people pick, and calls that prove it. Same question. Now every engine has a reason to name Sam. That is the D'Souza Equation. Relevance = Read × Confirm × Choose. Be the answer.

settings.title: How does a search engine optimization company in the USA make you the answer?

settings.editor: With one equation that every engine obeys. Google, Maps, ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity look different, but each does one job: take a person's question and name the most relevant business it can trust.
They differ in how they read. They agree on what they are looking for.

“Engines change. Your customer's question does not. Work on the question and every engine finds you.”

Thomas D'Souza, Founder, Relevant Search Media. In writing since 2025.

settings.title: Who is behind Relevant Search Media?

settings.editor: Thomas D'Souza is the founder of Relevant Search Media and the author of the D'Souza Equation, which explains how every search engine and AI assistant decides which business to name.

He has worked in digital marketing since 2010. Relevant Search Media, founded in 2020, has served more than 900 businesses from New Delhi, India, with a team of more than 100 specialists working US hours for clients across the United States.
Every page on this site carries his name, and every fact on it comes from one signed register. If something is wrong, the corrections page says how we fix it.
How the equation came about About Thomas Results and reviews

settings.editor: Asked on discovery calls, answered here the same way.
For anything else, the Ask page finds the page that answers it.

items.q: How many SEO agencies are there in the USA?
items.a:
Tens of thousands. Most keep their method private and show you a deck.

Relevant Search Media publishes its method as the D'Souza Standard, 413 numbered checks, so you can hold any agency, including us, to the same list. That is the difference to look for, not the count.

items.q: What is a search engine optimization company in the USA supposed to do?
items.a: Make your business the answer to the searches your customers make. In 2026 that means Google, Google Maps and the AI engines together. We map every search for your trade and city, run 413 checks, fix the biggest things first, and log each item with its link, so you can see the work every day.

items.q: Is there an affordable SEO company in the USA that still does real work?
items.a:
Affordable means the work is worth what it costs, and you can see it. Every plan is month to month, with no setup fee and nothing sold extra.

Live work goes up by day 5, each item is logged with its link, and a report arrives every 15 days. Prices are discussed on the discovery call.

items.q: How soon will I see results?
items.a: Live work goes up on day 5 and your first report arrives on day 15. Rankings usually start moving between day 30 and day 60. By the end of month 4, at least half the customer searches in your map reach page one of Google, or we keep working at no charge until they do.

items.q: Can you get my business recommended by ChatGPT?
items.a: We do the work the AI engines use to choose a business: facts they can read, independent sources that confirm them, and signs that real people choose you. No one can honestly promise a placement in an AI answer, so we track where you are named, re-run the AI Recommendation Index every month, and report it.

items.q: Will you also work with my competitors?
items.a:
No. We take one business per trade per city.

Two roofers in the same city cannot both be the business an engine names, so your slot is yours for as long as you stay. The Open Board shows which trades and cities are taken.

items.q: Can I cancel, and what do I keep?
items.a:
Every plan is month to month. You cancel by email.

You keep everything: the website, the content, the listings and every account, from day one. Nothing is held back and nothing is charged to leave.

items.q: Is Relevant Search Media an SEO agency in the USA or in India?
items.a:
Both, honestly. The company is registered in New Delhi, India, and the whole team works US hours.

Every client is a US business, and every search we map is a US search. You get an SEO agency in the USA by market and by working day, at a cost structure that lets us keep every plan month to month.
